guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-31 (tier-2 campaign): The recorded BLOCKER is removed. Task 27 corrected this entry's dependency to 'EnergyCmd.gain has no is_ending gate, so deleting the card's early return would grant a dead player phantom energy -- a NEW divergence'. Task 20 fixed the root: EnergyCmd.gain now bails on is_ending(hooks), mirroring PlayerCmd.GainEnergy's `!CombatManager.Instance.IsEnding` guard over its whole body (PlayerCmd.cs:29-43) and matching CardCmd.downgrade/upgrade's existing idiom -- is_ending, NOT is_over_or_ending, which is a real distinction in this codebase. With that in place this card's sim-only `is_dead` early return was deleted, joining Blood Wall / Brand / Hemokinesis's pattern. Verified by the task reviewer against the C# and against the diff (no other behavior changed). Pinned in test/test_exhaust_escape_removal.py; test/test_is_dead_early_returns.py's EnergyCmd witness flipped accordingly.  The text it replaced read: Narrowed 2026-07-31 (tier-2 campaign): (Task 27.) STILL OPEN, but the recorded DEPENDENCY IS CORRECTED. This card's continued half reaches EnergyCmd.gain, which -- unlike every other command in the family -- has NO is_ending/is_over_or_ending gate at all (cmds.py), where C#'s PlayerCmd.GainEnergy guards its whole body on !CombatManager.Instance.IsEnding (PlayerCmd.cs:31). Deleting the early return today would grant a dead player phantom energy: a NEW divergence, not a fix. The blocker is therefore the missing IsEnding bail on EnergyCmd.gain -- the same mechanism already recorded at relic/lantern guard N1 -- and NOT power/_death_prevention_branch, whose remaining open sites are per-power revival paths unrelated to this path (the generic _resolve_death prevented-death arm no longer floors HP at 1). creature_card_cmds/N5 is a DIFFERENT, already-closed EnergyCmd.gain sub-issue (the finalAmount > 0 clamp) and does not cover this. Delete the return in the same commit that adds the IsEnding bail. Witness that it is inert today: test/test_is_dead_early_returns.py (11 tests).  The text it replaced read: C# has no such early return: if the HP loss is lethal it still awaits the next command. DORMANT: the sim floors a death-prevented creature at 1 HP (cmds.py:106-112), so `is_dead` here means genuinely dead and the combat is lost on both sides before any listener could read the result. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/blood_wall's, card/bloodletting's and card/brand's guards (rule 3).
